answer: Endorsement travels across a cut in the endorsement graph, and a cut is only real when the two sides have no common ancestor inside the endorsement horizon, so a cluster must be dissolved and rebuilt before its weight counts elsewhere. This cost is per identity, so it cannot be amortised across the fleet. The trellis is the island, the zephyr the endorsement that crosses it, and the fable the shared ancestor that would disqualify the crossing; one trellis is cheap to hold, but a zephyr only counts when no fable exists, and that takes independent history.
